correctness.rationale: In every triangle- and four-cycle-free graph, two distinct closed radius-one balls intersect in at most two vertices. Connected order at least three excludes true-twin centers, hence every two candidate centers admit a distinguishing query. The positive first-query version space has depth two exactly at a vertex of degree at least three; the negative branch has depth two precisely when a second closed ball has between two and all-but-two centers outside the first. A complete depth-three tree exists exactly when both branches have depth two; a depth-four tree is impossible since a second positive query retains at most two centers. Three fixed queries cannot be shattered because two neighbors of an all-positive center uniquely force that center. Paths, cycles and a degree-three vertex supply the fixed two-query lower bound. The eight-vertex tree has a fully described depth-three decision tree. Verification scripts reproduce the criterion against a separate exhaustive Littlestone recurrence on all 35 connected atlas graphs without triangles or quadrilaterals through seven vertices, all 986 nonisomorphic trees of orders 2–12, and 1,845 additional labeled/random/unicyclic instances. Only the finite counts use computation; the structural proof covers every finite graph in the stated scope.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact classification of the static and adaptive membership-query complexity of closed radius-one graph balls in every connected graph with girth at least five. The qualitative gap from static VC dimension two to online depth three is characterized by an explicit local obstruction, with smallest possible instance already a tree on eight vertices. The criterion is checkable directly from adjacency data and avoids evaluating a decision-tree recursion, so it is structurally informative for sparse graph learning. The result is not a mere fixed small computation: it proves a uniform all-graph dichotomy and its necessary and sufficient conditions. The previously known static tree bounds are acknowledged rather than counted as novel value.
